BIOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: BIOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any substance that conducts electricity
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: CELL BIOLOGY AND BIODIVERSITY S.

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 0 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 50 °C

5. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

6. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Ice melting to water
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Milk souring
   D. Iron rusting

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support and Movement in Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Support and Movement in Animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support and Movement in Animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support and Movement in Animals.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support and Movement in Animals.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination 3.2 Support and Movement Page 12 of 38 1 STRAND 1.0: C.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination in Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination in Plants.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination in Plants.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination in Plants.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination in Plants.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Support in Plants? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Support in Plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Support in Plants.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Support in Plants.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Support in Plants.

11. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Response and Coordination in Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Response and Coordination in Animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Response and Coordination in Animals.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Response and Coordination in Animals.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Response and Coordination in Animals.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Response and Coordination 2.2 Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Response and Coordination in Plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Support and Movement 3.0 Anatomy and Physiology of Animals 3.1 Response and Coor and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Support in Plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
